formal_hypotheses: Deterministic partial edit transition system with a fixed action alphabet
Exact per-step event/weight receipts, blocked-word observability and initial output
Future client/demand language restricted to declared terminal observations and full receipts
Rights and stagewise old-client preservation included in the partial transition relation, not silently inferred from AST
Absolute vector cost monoid N^k and full receipts, not prematurely saturated accumulated scalar cost
claims_to_check: Equality of full edit-word receipt functions is a right-congruence for authorized action suffixes and admits a canonical minimal deterministic quotient (classical residual-language theorem).
Nine equivalence classes in authored 32-state finite rights/output/tag system, independently verified by word enumeration and partition refinement.
Every fixed-demand cost frontier over the declared observables is constant within each quotient block, but the quotient need not be minimal for any single demand.
Prematurely saturated cumulative-cost equivalence need not be right-congruent; retain residual cost/remaining budget in source state or per-step traces.
No architecture-source-only finite feature projection can guarantee future rights-sensitive repair forecasts where source-independent authority varies.
